bottlenecks.reading: Scarce input: datacenter power, land, permits and server capacity. MSFT states electricity generation, transmission and grid connection are capacity constrained in many regions, that its capacity build depends on land, zoning and permits, and that demand above available capacity limits its ability to serve customers. Others adding capacity are the other hyperscalers; how long the shortage lasts is not stated in the filing (gap).
Paid demand shown in MSFT own numbers: Azure revenue $33,165m vs $22,384m a year earlier (+48%), Microsoft Cloud $63.9bn (+30%), commercial remaining performance obligation $677bn (+73%).

The 10-Q warns demand for cloud and AI is hard to forecast and that overestimated demand or misaligned capacity may cause underutilization and asset impairment; operating costs and margins pressured by datacenter and device investment. Counter-risk to the shortage reading.
Hypothesis: AI strategy depends on third-party model partners, many of whom also compete with MSFT (10-Q risk factor); the OpenAI dependency is not sized in this lane.

market_direction.reading: Demand for MSFT cloud and AI is rising faster than MSFT can supply it, on its own numbers: Azure revenue +48% y/y in Q1 FY2027 (guided +49% to +50% constant currency for Q2 FY2027), Microsoft Cloud $63.9bn +30%, commercial remaining performance obligation $677bn +73% with about 30% to be recognized in the next 12 months. The 10-Q itself warns AI demand is hard to forecast and over-building could leave assets underused. No regulator, industry study or buyer filing was retrieved, so the market size outside MSFT is not measured here.

bottleneck_potential.reading: MSFT is not a bottleneck supplier; it is a capacity holder that is itself constrained by power, land, permits and GPUs (10-K/10-Q risk factors). Its edge is the capacity it has locked in: $364.6bn of datacenter leases not yet commenced at 2026-09-30 (up from $329.1bn at 2026-06-30, commencing FY27-FY34), $194.1bn purchase commitments, capex including finance leases $45.2bn in Q1 FY2027 and guided above $50bn in Q2. The other hyperscalers (Amazon, Alphabet, Oracle) add capacity in parallel; how long the shortage lasts is not stated by any source here (gap).

share_trajectory.reading: Azure at +48% grows far faster than the whole-company revenue of Amazon (+12.4% FY2025), Alphabet (+15.1% FY2025) and Oracle (+17.4% FY2026), which suggests MSFT is gaining cloud share, but AWS, Google Cloud and OCI segment revenue and any attributed share study were not retrieved, so no share conclusion is drawn.

competitive_position.reading: On the numbers retrieved MSFT is the most profitable of the named competitors: FY2026 operating margin 46.8% (155.2 of 331.8bn) and revenue growth 17.8%, against whole-company operating margins of 32.0% at Alphabet, 30.6% at Oracle and 11.2% at Amazon (whole companies, not the competing segments). Breadth is its advantage: Microsoft 365 (seats +6%, revenue per user up on Copilot and E5) plus Azure plus the 24% OpenAI stake. Weak spots: Windows OEM and Devices -22% and Xbox content -2% in Q1 FY2027.

threats.reading: 1) Counterparty: OpenAI is 10.8% of Q1 FY2027 revenue ($10.0bn), owes $7.2bn, and the amended agreement (April 2026, press) lets it use other clouds. 2) Over-build: capex rose from $20.6bn (FY2021) to $115.9bn (FY2026) with $364.6bn of leases still to start; if AI demand or pricing disappoints, those are fixed costs (10-Q risk factor). 3) Substitution: customers may shift AI workloads to competing platforms, on-premises or local models (10-Q). 4) Regulation: competition authorities in the EU, UK, US and China; legal accruals $582m are small, while the IRS seeks $28.9bn plus penalties and interest on transfer pricing for 2004-2013 (10-Q).

bear.event_he: OpenAI, שמהווה כ-11% מההכנסות וממומנת בחלקה על ידי מיקרוסופט (12 מיליארד דולר כבר הועברו), מקצצת את ההוצאה על Azure או מתקשה לשלם (יתרת חוב של 7.2 מיליארד דולר).
צבר ההזמנות מתברר כתלוי ב-OpenAI: הצבר המסחרי צמח ב-84% בשנת 2026 אבל רק ב-25% בלי OpenAI, כך שקיצוץ של OpenAI פוגע בצמיחה העתידית הרבה יותר מחלקה של 11% בהכנסות של היום.
הביקוש ל-AI מתברר כנמוך מהקיבולת שנבנתה: 364.6 מיליארד דולר של חכירות מרכזי נתונים שעוד לא התחילו ו-169 מיליארד התחייבויות רכש לשנה הקרובה הופכים לעלות קבועה, והשוליים יורדים.
שוק המחשבים ממשיך להיחלש: Windows OEM ומכשירים ירדו 22% ברבעון, ותחום המכשירים והצרכנים מתכווץ.

מחירי שירותי AI יורדים בגלל תחרות של AWS, Google Cloud ו-Oracle על אותם לקוחות. (בתרחיש הזה התשואה על ההון החדש היא כ-14%, מתחת לכל שנה ברקורד של החברה, ומכפיל הרווח יורד מתחת לשפל של 5 השנים: זו הנחת לחץ, לא נתון.)

base.event_he: ברבעון השני של FY2027 ההכנסות בטווח ההנחיה, 96.0-97.1 מיליארד דולר, ו-Azure צומח 49%-50%.
כ-30% מהצבר החוזי של 677 מיליארד דולר (כ-203 מיליארד) הופכים להכנסה בתוך 12 חודשים.
ההשקעות נשארות מעל 50 מיליארד דולר לרבעון, והפחת העולה מוריד את שולי הרווח הגולמי בהדרגה.

bull.event_he: יכולת המחשוב של צד שלישי (GPU) שנדחתה למחצית השנייה של FY2027 מגיעה, והביקוש שעולה על ההיצע הופך להכנסות.
הצבר החוזי המסחרי, שגדל 73% בשנה, ממשיך לגדול ו-Azure נשאר מעל 40% צמיחה גם ב-FY2028.
Copilot וסוכני AI מתרחבים בבסיס לקוחות Microsoft 365 (מספר הלקוחות עם יותר מ-50 אלף רישיונות גדל פי 8), ומוסיפים הכנסה בשוליים גבוהים.

growth_anchor.reason: Own run rate: Q1 FY2027 revenue +18.8% y/y and the Q2 guide midpoint +18.8% (96.55B vs 81.27B). Azure (about 36% of revenue) grows 48% and is guided 49-50%; the rest grows mid-single digits (Windows OEM -22%). Base 17%: Azure decelerates on a larger base toward the mid-30s while ~30% of the 677B commercial RPO (about 203B) is recognized within 12 months, so contracted demand covers more than half of next year's revenue. Bull 23%: the GPU capacity that slipped into H2 FY2027 arrives and RPO (+73%) converts with Azure above 40%. Bear 8%: OpenAI (10.8% of revenue, partly funded by MSFT, and most of the backlog growth: commercial RPO +84% in FY2026 but +25% excluding OpenAI) flattens its spend and Azure falls to 15-20% growth while the consumer/PC lines keep shrinking. Consensus (dated 2026-11-01) is not citable until 2026-11-03 and is not used.

mature_margin.reason: Operating margin was 41.6%-46.8% in FY2021-FY2026 (median 44.6%), 49.8% in Q1 FY2027 (flag peak_margin_run_rate) and about 46.8% implied by the Q2 guide. Base 44%: the history median, because depreciation of mostly short-lived AI servers (D&A 34.3B in FY2026 vs 22.0B in FY2025, capex doubling) keeps eating the gross margin (-125 bp y/y). Bull 48%: Q1-level operating leverage (opex +6% vs revenue +19%) persists. Bear 38%: AI pricing falls while the depreciation and 364.6B of not-yet-commenced leases are fixed, taking the margin below the FY2021 low.

sales_to_capital.reason: Lease-inclusive basis, consistent with the finance-lease liabilities deducted as debt: incremental revenue / (cash capex + finance-lease ROU additions from the 10-K/10-Q lease note - D&A). FY2024-FY2026: 119.9B / 210.2B = 0.57; FY2026 0.47 (50.1B / 106.3B), FY2025 0.58, FY2024 0.81. Base 0.55: near the three-year figure, slightly below it because capex keeps rising (Q1 FY2027 cash PP&E 39.4B plus 5.2B finance leases; CY2026 capex guided ~175B). Bear 0.42: below the FY2026 low of 0.47 (capex above 50B a quarter while growth slows). Bull 0.75: capex flattens as the fleet fills and conversion moves back toward FY2024 (0.81). Future datacenter leases shift to operating leases (outside capex, inside operating costs), and the 364.6B of leases not yet commenced are outside this capital base: their cost is carried in the margin lever, not here.

tax_rate.reason: Management guides an effective tax rate of about 20% for Q1 and Q2 FY2027; held in every scenario.

sbc_pct.reason: SBC 12.4B = 3.7% of FY2026 revenue (4.25% FY2025, 4.4% FY2024, falling as revenue outgrows grants); charged as a real cost at the latest level.

terminal_roic.reason: One return on capital for the DCF and the company path (position/path.json roic bear 0.14 / base 0.22 / bull 0.31). Lease-inclusive after-tax (20%) incremental ROIC from MSFT's own figures: FY2024-FY2026 53.4B / 210.2B = 0.25, FY2026 0.20, FY2025 0.24. Base 0.22: inside that record, below the three-year figure because the newest year is the lowest. Bull 0.31: the company's overall return on invested capital, reached if the new AI capacity earns like the existing business. Bear 0.14: a stress hypothesis below anything in the record (lowest year 0.20), for AI overcapacity and price competition; not evidenced, hence analyst tier.

bear.reason_he: בתרחיש הדובי ההון שמושקע ב-AI (השקעות הוניות של 116 מיליארד דולר בשנה האחרונה ויותר מ-50 מיליארד דולר ברבעון לפי ההנחיה, ועוד התחייבויות חכירה של 443 מיליארד דולר שאינן בחישוב ההון) לא מתמלא בלקוחות משלמים או תלוי מדי ב-OpenAI, ולכן התשואה על ההון הנוסף יורדת לכ-14%: עדיין מעל עלות ההון, אבל רחוק מ-31% של היום. תשואה נמוכה על הצמיחה פירושה שהצמיחה שווה פחות, ולכן המכפיל נמוך.

base.reason_he: התשואה על ההון הנוסף של מיקרוסופט ב-3 השנים האחרונות הייתה כ-24% (רווח תפעולי עלה מ-88.5 ל-155.2 מיליארד דולר, וההון המושקע גדל מהר), והתשואה הכוללת ירדה מכ-38% בשנת 2022 ל-31% בשנת 2026 בגלל בניית חוות השרתים. ההנחה היא כ-22% על ההון החדש (ההון כולל מוניטין, החכירות לא כלולות ולכן נלקח מעט פחות): תשואה גבוהה בהרבה מעלות ההון שמצדיקה מכפיל גבוה, שיורד בהדרגה ככל שהצמיחה מאטה.

bull.reason_he: בתרחיש השורי הקיבולת החדשה מתמלאת בביקוש משלם: Azure צמחה 48% ברבעון האחרון, ההנחיה לרבעון הבא היא 49%-50%, וענן מיקרוסופט צמח 30% ל-63.9 מיליארד דולר. אז ההון החדש מרוויח כמו העסק הקיים, כ-31% (התשואה של שנת 2026), ולא יותר כי זו כבר תשואה אחרי ירידה מ-38%. תשואה כזו על הצמיחה מצדיקה מכפיל גבוה שנשאר גבוה.

key_risk.reading_he: מיקרוסופט משקיעה כ-45-50 מיליארד דולר ברבעון ומתחייבת ל-364.6 מיליארד דולר חכירות מרכזי נתונים נוספות, בעוד לקוח אחד, OpenAI, הוא כ-11% מההכנסות, מקבל ממנה מימון, ואחראי לרוב הגידול בצבר ההזמנות: הצבר המסחרי צמח ב-84% בשנה, אבל רק ב-25% בלי OpenAI. אם הביקוש של OpenAI או של שוק ה-AI נחלש, ההכנסות מאטות אבל עלויות הפחת והחכירות נשארות, והתזרים החופשי (כבר ירד ל-20% מההכנסות) נשחק.

commercial remaining performance obligation Q3 FY2027 (USD)

moat.note: Sources evidenced: an installed enterprise base (Microsoft 365 seats +6% in FY2026 with rising revenue per user) and scale in cloud. Operating margin 46.8% in FY2026 vs whole-company 32.0% Alphabet, 30.6% Oracle, 11.2% Amazon; ROIC 31% last year (average 34%) against an 8% cost-of-capital reference. Segment margins of the competitors not retrieved.

switching_costs.note: Commercial RPO $677bn with weighted duration 2.3 years: customers commit for years; Microsoft 365 seats still grew 6% in FY2026. No churn or net retention rate is disclosed.

pricing_power.note: Microsoft 365 commercial cloud +17% in Q1 FY2027, driven by higher revenue per user (upsell to Copilot, E5 and E7) on top of 6% seat growth in FY2026. The 10-Q warns AI pricing must recover its costs and that competition affects pricing.

customer_concentration.note: OpenAI is 10.8% of Q1 FY2027 revenue with a $7.2bn receivable and is also a 24% equity-method investee; no other customer above 10% in FY2024-FY2026. OpenAI's share of RPO is not disclosed (gap).

market_size.note: MSFT's own contracted demand ($677bn commercial RPO, +73%) and Azure +48% accelerating to a guided +49-50%; no external market-size study retrieved.

competition.note: Intense competition in every market (10-K Item 1A); Amazon, Alphabet and Oracle are well-funded and adding AI capacity, and several AI model partners also compete. MSFT leads on margin but Windows OEM (-22%) and Xbox (-2%) are shrinking.

substitutes.note: The 10-Q lists the shift of AI workloads to competing platforms, on-premises or local deployments as a risk; no measured loss yet (Azure +48%).

management.note: Q1 FY2027 delivered above the company's own guidance: revenue $92.3bn vs guided $89.85-90.95bn, Azure +48% vs guided about +45% constant currency. One quarter checked; the multi-quarter track-record ratio was not computed (auto.json track_record null).

capital_allocation.note: Buybacks $22.3bn exceed SBC $12.4bn in FY2026; diluted shares fell from 7,608m (FY2021) to 7,446m. But capex $115.9bn took 63% of $182.9bn operating cash flow in FY2026, FCF margin fell from 33% (FY2021) to 20%, and incremental ROIC (23.6%) is below the average (34%). The Activision purchase (goodwill +$51bn in FY2024) has no evidenced return yet: Xbox content -2%.

regulation.note: Scrutiny by EU, UK, US and China competition authorities; accrued legal liabilities $582m with about $400m reasonably possible beyond it; partial dismissal of a ChatGPT-user antitrust suit. Larger item: IRS transfer-pricing claim of $28.9bn plus penalties and interest (2004-2013), which MSFT says its allowances cover.

technology_ai.note: Paid AI adoption is in the numbers: Azure +48% and Microsoft 365 revenue per user up on Copilot; 24% as-converted OpenAI stake. Dependence on third-party model partners who also compete is a stated risk.

geopolitics.note: US 53.6% of Q1 FY2027 revenue, no other country above 10%; AI export-control and tariff risks are named in the filings but not sized; Taiwan/China supply share not disclosed (gap).

cyclical.reason: Revenue grew every year FY2021-FY2026 and operating margin stayed within 41.6%-46.8%; recurring cloud and subscription revenue backed by a 677B commercial RPO. The AI capacity build carries an overbuild risk (10-Q risk factor), handled in the bear, not an industry price cycle.

debt_like_claims.reason: Total finance lease liabilities 70,973M at 2026-09-30 (other current liabilities 5,005M + other long-term liabilities 65,968M; 10-Q lease note). They are outside the 35.5B debt lines and their payments are amortisation and interest, not operating costs.
